# Audit presentation fixtures

## Historical landing example

`landing-v1.3-provenance.json` and `landing-v1.3-binding.json` are complete,
unaltered certificate objects extracted from the published
[v1.3.0 research edition](https://github.com/Azzbee/ariadne-bio/releases/tag/v1.3.0).
They anchor the landing page's explicitly recorded Marimastat / rheumatoid
arthritis example to its original fitted model. They are not regenerated by a
new model fit.

Extraction was checked against the sealed `ariadne-research-edition.zip`, its
`SHA256SUMS`, and a separately downloaded identical public release archive:

- Archive SHA-256: `fa882458fb629b677cf6ef4e064aff3732aea42b1f6fc6fc8627da7985715b31`.
- Archive source commit: `4aaca9de9080ff5f5b114b8bd965fc1a459408dd`.
- Archive source tree: `6625007f855137aaaa2526aebd802f28b5a8a369`.
- Case member: `data/cases/rheumatoid-arthritis-disease-doid-7148.json`.
- Case member SHA-256: `e962f39683f5927d83b5df787cca7daee527b401ea9d4bb8c4e49af09da2cff7` (7,804,548 bytes), also checked against the archive's snapshot manifest.
- Model identity: `311897fb3678a7885b8ddb7d63becfe990860bfb3c39cb6195166bad531d14f3`.

| Fixture | Original case lookup | Certificate SHA-256 | Fixture bytes SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `landing-v1.3-provenance.json` | `provenance_audits["Compound::DB00786"]["10:1"]` | `73b4f7cc762e8e362e1d2fc0c753b290bbee3f051eb5a3df9809ca9de58a60e2` | `9353fbe91855eee9021544da862d9bee01840396c010f91aa85fe45523c52e8e` |
| `landing-v1.3-binding.json` | `audits["Compound::DB00786"]["10:2"]` | `75a176e19f2f3948cf1758b301f27deceba6e2269a4aaa1d549d5d17dbcd172c` | `816b8f502b8cd15be768b5ef70ec41c8ac047ea0bcffebbb01121697dc8bd570` |

The extraction preserves every JSON value and the original certificate seals;
only whitespace is reformatted with two-space indentation and a final newline.
Both extracted files also passed `python -m scripts.verify_audit` against their
matching prepared graph and original model: the binding verifier replayed one
distinct witness, and the provenance verifier replayed two. Those commands
recomputed the bounds and checked full edited-matrix witnesses; fixture byte
hashes and browser structural checks alone do not establish mathematical validity.
`landing.test.js` always checks both fixture byte hashes, validates both complete
certificate structures, and compares the displayed identity, ranks, path counts,
source membership and affected-record counts with these historical results.
The historical check runs even when no generated snapshot is present.

The generated `frontend/data` snapshot has a separate role: it binds to the model
used for that particular export, which may be a fresh CI fit. All existing checks
in `snapshot.test.js` continue to test that snapshot's actual manifests,
certificates, coverage and recorded verification. A fresh model identity must not
be compared with the landing example's historical model identity.

## Joint audit presentation

`mixed-marimastat.json` is an actual certificate from `MixedAuditor`, generated
from the prepared reference graph and fitted model for Marimastat / rheumatoid
arthritis, with top-k 10 and group/record budgets 1+1. The engine's independent
edited-matrix verification returned `valid: true` during fixture generation.
Its embedded identities bind the complete graph/model/scorer and source-group map.

The certificate SHA-256 is
`dd704f9f3ab9a17766e66fb2ed05dcd3897c52e63bf05bb0a60e37f78348a9c8`.
Worst supported ranks across (0,0), (0,1), (1,0), (1,1) are 1, 1, 1,096, 1,096;
the joint cell also has a separate support-loss witness. The presentation tests
keep that distinction intact and intentionally alter copies to test rejection.

Mock verification responses inside unit tests test transport and asynchronous
state handling. They are explicitly unit fixtures and are not publication
evidence. Actual exported snapshots and release verification carry independently
executed records.
